questions.prompt: Some people say India should spend less on space missions and more on problems at home. Give one argument for and one against continuing space missions, and your own view.
questions.modelAnswer: For continuing: satellites give weather forecasts that save lives in cyclones, support farming, mapping, communication and navigation; missions inspire students into science; they create jobs and technology, and ISRO’s missions are known for low cost. Against: the money could fund health, education or clean water directly. My view: India should continue, because much space spending (weather and communication satellites) directly helps people on Earth, while making sure the budget is balanced and benefits are shared.
questions.explain: Criterion D: weigh the costs and benefits of science.

questions.text: The average distance from Earth to the Sun, about 150 million km, is called one ___ unit (AU).
